page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c9i.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. The instance is paired with 192.0 GB of system memory, creating a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No discrete GPU accelerators are integrated into this hardware profile.

The server configuration does not include local storage, requiring cloud storage volumes across network interfaces for persistent data needs. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps. The instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured elastic network interfaces or NAT gateways for external routing.

By prioritizing core count over large memory capacity, the instance offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-intensive tasks where high RAM-to-vCPU ratios would result in idle memory resources. The architecture trades local storage IOPS for network-attached storage flexibility. The platform fits parallel compute pipelines, distributed code compilation, video transcoding, scientific simulation, batch analytics, and large-scale web application serving.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage, relying on external network-attached storage for persistent workloads, and includes no discrete GPU accelerators. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 32 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default. It is well matched for compute-bound workloads, such as distributed code compilation, financial simulation, compute-intensive continuous integration tasks, batch processing, and large-scale web serving tiers.
